injections.name: an-enum-that-may-not-be-exhausted-is-held-to-exhaustiveness
injections.why: R1282 — this is the gate's own first mistake, kept as evidence. The walk excluded enums from OUTSIDE the workspace and not enums this tree marks `#[non_exhaustive]`, so it found `mnemosyne-render::door_label` naming all three `Door` variants beside a catch-all — and the repair it licensed DID NOT BUILD, because rustc requires that wildcard in every crate but the one defining the enum. Dropping the attribute check puts that finding back: a gate that refuses the code the compiler demands is one people learn to ignore, and there are 32 such enums in this tree for it to be wrong about

injections.name: a-sixth-orphan-kind-joins-neither-ledger
injections.why: R1282 — 2 of 5 variants named, `_ => {}`, and the direction is the one that reads as compliance: a new `OrphanKind` falls into it, contributes to neither ledger set, and the difference against the actual orphans then reports it as a new orphan or as one nobody registered. The orphan ledger is what `validate-workspace` subtracts before saying `new = +0`

injections.name: a-new-verdict-is-refused-without-being-read
injections.why: R1282 — 4 of 7 named, and this is the match R1279 measured: adding a `LockVerdict` variant compiled at every reader in the tree because this was the only `match` over it and it ended in `other =>`. Refusing was the right DIRECTION and still the wrong SHAPE — the catch-all is what stopped the compiler asking the one reader that has to decide

injections.name: the-walk-finds-no-enums-and-calls-the-tree-clean
injections.why: R1282 — the reader half. A walk that collected no enum definitions would recognise no match as being over one of this workspace's enums, find nothing, and pass; that is the shape of every gate this repository has caught reporting a clean answer because it did not look. The denominators are asserted for exactly this, and this is what says the assertion fires rather than decorating the test
